findings.text: newest_delivered_review takes its order from stored_records_for_run, which sorts staged files by mtime (reckon/crew/review_records.py:81). A disposition written onto an older round with --review is an in-place rewrite that moves that file's mtime past the newer round's, so the next un-named call reads the older round as the newest delivered review and stops refusing: the guard decays from 'newest delivered' to 'newest written'. The repository already owns a review ordering by dispatch stamp (review_lifecycle._dispatch_time), which a rewrite does not move.

The crew tool's dispose argument map carries no review parameter, so the remedy the new refusal names (--review <review run id>) cannot be supplied through the tool surface, and a coordinator who reaches the refusal through the tool is told to run a flag that surface cannot pass; reckon/mcp_crew_actions.py:210 has no default for it either.

dispose_commands renders the fold and exempt invocations a duty row hands a coordinator without --review, so in the multi-round case this node exists for, the command a duty prints is now refused and no duty rendering names the newer review run.
